title: SoftHold: ephemeral overage control to deprioritize non-critical requests before hard quota throttles
creator: Aria Chen
description: Problem: Tenants occasionally generate short spikes that exhaust burst buckets and immediately hit hard throttles (429). This causes poor UX for non-essential background workloads while critical foreground requests could continue if capacity existed. We need a mechanism that: 1) detects imminent quota exhaustion in real-time, 2) applies a temporary, tenant-scoped 'softhold' that deprioritizes or delays non-critical requests rather than immediately returning hard throttles, 3) is configurable per-tenant and compatible with reserved capacity commitments, and 4) leaves clear audit trails and billing semantics.
context: Related work: several incidents in Q4 where analytics pipelines hit burst buckets and customer-facing APIs degraded. Existing linear tickets cover hard-reset reconciliation and reserved pool leakage, but there is no live mitigation that buys time while alerts and autoscaling react. This feature should integrate with Smart Routing and the runtime's batching/queueing layer.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can detect when tenant burst budget is within X% (configurable, default 90%) of exhaustion and enter a softhold state for that tenant
Softhold enforces policy at request-routing layer: mark low-priority requests to be queued/delayed with exponential backoff or converted to 'best-effort' responses instead of immediate 429s
High-priority requests (flags: critical=true or oauth scope) are exempted or served with preference and still count against quota
Per-tenant configuration available in Console: threshold, classification rules (header-based or path-based), and allowed hold duration
Telemetry captures softhold events: start/end timestamps, requests affected, estimated token savings, and links to cost dashboard
Automated tests simulate out-of-order usage events and verify no double-counting of saved tokens or billing discrepancies
Feature can be safely rolled back via a feature flag and does not affect billing consistency for reserved capacity customers
design_notes: Softhold is a transient, policy-driven state (not a persistent quota change). It is advisory to the serving runtime and is enforced at the edge routing layer where per-tenant token accounting is freshest

Classification: requests are labeled as critical or non-critical via a priority header set by SDKs or by route patterns configured in Console. Default heuristic: /v1/chat and function calls -> high priority; batch ingestion endpoints -> low priority
Decision engine: simple threshold-based detector in the quota service that publishes 'softhold' signal via the existing tenant push channel. Signal includes TTL and suggested backoff parameters

Enforcement model options evaluated: 1) immediate 429 -> rejected (current), 2) queue + delayed execution (adds latency), 3) downgrade to lower-cost model/quantized path, 4) return cached/placeholder response. We'll implement 2 + 3 initially

Billing semantics: tokens consumed when requests are executed. If a request is queued and later executed, consumption is billed as normal. If the request is dropped due to softhold TTL expiry, we record a 'softhold-dropped' event for audit but do not bill. Reserved capacity tenants get a configurable tolerance window so softhold does not mistakenly block guaranteed throughput
Observability: new dashboard widgets: active softholds, per-tenant hold history, estimated token savings, and false-positive rate metric (requests marked low-priority but user considered blocked)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API + runtime): implement detector in quota-service + publish softhold signals to routing cache (2wk)
Phase 2 (enforcement): routing layer honors softhold signals; low-priority requests are queued with exponential backoff and equipped with 'X-SoftHold: true' header for downstream debugging (2wk)
Phase 3 (console + config): add per-tenant softhold configuration UI and default policies; expose metrics (1wk)
Phase 4 (safety + billing): add audit events, verify billing integration with usage ledger, and implement rollback feature flagging (1wk)
Phase 5 (pilot + rollout): enable for a small cohort of willing Reserved customers; monitor KPIs for 2 weeks then broad rollout

ENG: routing-edge - implement queueing + backoff handlers and header propagation (Rina)

Docs: SDK/HTTP header docs and recommended priority annotation examples (DevRel)
Legal/Security: review for compliance where audit trail is required (Security)
Pilot: enroll 3 reserved customers and run 2-week pilot (Customer Success)
Rollback: ensure feature flagging and emergency kill switch in routing (Ops)
testing_plan: Unit tests for detector logic with synthetic token streams
Integration tests: multi-region gateway + delayed usage event ingestion scenarios
Chaos test: kill quota-service momentarily and verify routing defaults to safe behavior (immediate hard throttle) rather than allowing overconsumption
Billing reconciliation test: create scenario where queued requests are executed across a day boundary and assert ledger correctness
Pilot smoke tests with customer workloads (sample traffic replay)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal testing on staging cluster behind feature flag
Stage 1: enable for 5% of internal production traffic for 48 hours; monitor failover metrics
Stage 2: pilot with 3 reserved customers (opt-in) for 2 weeks
Stage 3: gradual ramp to all tenants with per-tenant opt-out for first month
Fallback: feature flag off and routing reverts to existing hard-throttle behavior
observability_kpis: softhold_start_rate: number of softhold enters per hour
false_positive_rate: fraction of holds where critical traffic was impacted
billing_delta: tokens saved vs. billed during holds
customer_error_increase: delta in 5xx/4xx for critical endpoints during holds

estimated_savings_note: Conservative estimate: 10-20% reduction in hard-throttle incidents for background workloads; worth pilot for large reserved tenants
privacy_considerations: Softhold audit logs contain tenant usage metadata. Ensure PII is not included and logs respect retention policies. Security review required.
